source.title: Strabane Chronicle, 23 May 1964, p. 2 ("Two contests likely in Omagh Rural: Co. councillors get a clear field")
source.publisher: Strabane Chronicle (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: the full nomination list read in the Strabane Chronicle of 23 May 1964 and the Castlegore count in the Ulster Herald of 13 June 1964, cross-checked against the Irish News of 5 June 1964 (247 to 237, majority 10, electorate 544, total poll 485, one spoiled paper).

note: Triennial election of Castlederg Rural District Council, polled Thursday 4 June 1964. There was one contest, in Castlegore, the first in the district for thirty years; the other divisions were uncontested and are listed as the nomination report prints them. The returning officer's count at Castlederg was held on the night of the poll. Ardarver, Clunahill and Corgary are added from the Returning Officer's Notice of Result (Ulster Herald, 13 June 1964, p. 8), which names their members as retired members deemed to be re-elected (7 Nov 2026). James Verner. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Killeen' to Killen (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the 1911 DED map (Castlederg Rural District) and the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-69 name the DED Killen; the rounds were filed as Killen (1924, 1927, 1930, 1933, 1936, 1939, 1946, 1949, 1952, 1955, 1958, 1961, 1967); Killeen (1964). This round was filed as 'Killeen', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (killeen) answers with a redirect to this one.
